column1: # Y GRID -- extend the WINNING schedule past 90 epochs: Q02 base x epochs {120, 150} x eta_min {1e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4}
# WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO ACHIEVE OVERALL
# Predict a perturbation's effect in a cellular context where that perturbation was never
# measured, from a single control cell. Headline: split-half paired `pearson_delta` on the
# 611-perturbation rhj_fewshot HepG2 cohort, 6,983-gene axis, cell-eval 0.6.0, uncalibrated.
# WHAT THIS GRID ANSWERS
# F-sched2 found that `epochs` is the strongest lever in the campaign and `eta_min` is inert
# across 1e-7...1e-4. Its best arm, W23 (Q02, 90 ep, eta_min 1e-5) = 0.3959, is the campaign
# best. But the series DECELERATES: Q02 gains +0.0150 from 30->60 and only +0.0025 from
# 60->90. THIS GRID ASKS WHETHER THE EPOCHS AXIS IS STILL LIVE PAST 90, and re-tests the
# `eta_min` axis at a length where the floor could finally matter -- the cosine spends
# proportionally longer near its floor as the schedule lengthens.
# WHAT IS VARIED / HELD FIXED
# VARIED: epochs (120, 150) x eta_min (1e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4).
# HELD FIXED: the Q02 loss composition exactly as W23 -- smooth_l1 + delta_cos 0.5 +
#   delta_mag 0.01363 + latent MSE (delta_z) 0.0044, no VICReg, no recon split. Everything
#   else is arm s313: adjacency_map, batch 2048, lr 1e-3, decoder_lr 1e-3, cosine schedule,
#   warmup 5 epochs, seed 42.
# WHY THESE THREE eta_min VALUES
# lr = 1e-3 AND decoder_lr = 1e-3 in this base, so eta_min must stay strictly below 1e-3 or
# the cosine never decays at all. 1e-7...1e-4 is MEASURED FLAT (F-sched2: within-row spread
# 0.0006-0.0033 pearson_delta, no monotone direction), so re-spending three values inside that
# band buys nothing. 1e-5 and 1e-4 are kept as CONTINUITY CONTROLS against W23 and W24; the
# third, 3e-4, is the only untested regime -- the LR never falls below 0.3x peak.
# ⚠️ W23's SELECTED weights sit at EPOCH 60 OF 90 (`best_model.pth` holds epoch=60, val
# pearson_delta 0.4419; the final 30 epochs never beat it). So the 90-over-60 gain was NOT
# "more steps" -- it was the GENTLER COSINE SLOPE that a 90-epoch schedule gives at epoch 60.
# That is the mechanism these arms extend. Expect their useful checkpoint at ~2/3 of the
# schedule too, i.e. ~epoch 80 (120 ep) and ~epoch 100 (150 ep), not at the end.
# HOW TO READ THE RESULT -- PRE-REGISTERED, before any number is seen
# Y01/Y04 > 0.3959 by >=0.002 at 4-5/5 -> the epochs axis is STILL LIVE past 90; keep climbing.
# Y01/Y04 ~ 0.3959 (|delta| < 0.002)   -> 90 IS THE PLATEAU and the decelerating series
#                                         (+0.0150, +0.0025) has converged. Stop tuning length.
# Y01 > Y04                            -> 120 is the optimum and 150 over-trains.
# Y03/Y06 (3e-4) beats the 1e-5 column -> the flat eta_min surface was flat only because the
#                                         whole tested band was too low to matter; the floor
#                                         becomes a real knob at long schedules.
# disc_l1 keeps rising with length while pearson_delta plateaus -> length TRADES discrimination
#                                         against delta correlation, and the pick depends on
#                                         which metric is the target.
# ANCHORS (part of the context, not a footnote) -- test, uncalibrated, 5/5 splits
# ctrlcell -0.0018 · ctrlmean 0.0016 · meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 · experimental 0.3722
# Directions: pearson_delta UP · mae DOWN (it is an ERROR) · ovl@N UP · disc_l1 UP (chance 0.5).
# COST, MEASURED (W23: 41 s/epoch, 1:15:14 wall for 90 ep incl. eval)
# 120 ep ~= 1 h 40 · 150 ep ~= 2 h 05 -> ⚠️ SUBMIT WITH --time=04:00:00; the sbatch default of
# 02:00:00 WOULD KILL THE 150-EPOCH ARMS a few minutes from the end. 6 arms ~= 11 GPU-h train,
# plus 30 eval tasks at ~9 min on a %6 throttle (F-infra1) ~= 4.5 GPU-h.
#   GRID=scripts/grids/rhj_epochs_ext.tsv \
#   sbatch --qos=vco --wckey=vco --time=04:00:00 --array=0-5 scripts/slurm/rhj_loss_sweep.sbatch
# ⚠️ EPOCHS AND ETA_MIN ARE PER-ROW (columns 20-21). The EPOCHS/ETA_MIN env vars are global to
# a job and cannot express a grid that varies them.
